title: When the Monsoon Wakes
premise: Hazel Amberdale, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted after a rescue gone wrong, is coerced by a shadowy ministry official into finding a government survey team that vanished in the Khumbal Range, leaving intact gear and no tracks. Leading a small recovery party, she discovers the team found something buried in the ice — evidence of an old massacre covered up by the very government that hired her — and that one survivor is hiding with it. Hunted by the official's own cleanup crew and racing the closing monsoon, Hazel must choose between delivering the survivor and the secret home as ordered, or exposing the truth and burning what's left of her name. She chooses exposure: she gets the survivor down the mountain alive, releases the evidence to a journalist, and walks out of the valley into arrest — finally at peace with who she is.
about_author: B. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting high-altitude surveys before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where the weather still dictates the writing schedule.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Working a low-season trek in the border town of Rungli, Hazel measures her life in distances walked since the disaster that got her blacklisted seven years ago. A letter arrives summoning her to the district office. Beat: restless isolation cracked open by an unwelcome summons.

chapters.title: The Man from the Ministry
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Official Dev Rathore offers her a deal: guide a recovery team to find the vanished Meridian Survey, or face extradition on old charges. He shows her photos of abandoned gear — tents pitched, stoves cold, no tracks. Beat: trapped, she signs; the reader senses the trap has teeth.

chapters.title: A Party of Five
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She meets her team: earnest young surveyor Tomas, taciturn porter Dorje, ministry liaison Priya, and ex-army medic Kwan. Trust is thin; everyone has orders they won't share. Beat: uneasy alliance formed under pressure of the short weather window.

chapters.title: The Last Village
chapters.summary: Dorje's POV. At the final settlement before the high country, villagers refuse to speak of the mountain, but an old woman presses a copper amulet into Dorje's hand and says the ice 'keeps its debts.' Beat: dread seeded; the mountain has a history someone wants forgotten.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The party reaches the abandoned camp: everything intact, food untouched, boots left behind. Hazel reads the site like a crime scene and concludes the team walked out barefoot, together, uphill — impossible. Beat: rational competence colliding with the uncanny.

chapters.title: Tracks That End
chapters.summary: Kwan's POV. Following faint traces above camp, Kwan finds a single boot print pressed into glacial ice — then nothing for two hundred meters, then all six surveyors' names carved into a rockface. Beat: fear becomes contagious; the mission stops being a search.

chapters.title: What Priya Carries
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In her tent, Priya decrypts a second set of orders: if the survey's findings are recoverable, recover them; if not, ensure they aren't. She looks at Hazel sleeping and wonders which category Hazel falls into. Beat: the reader learns the recovery team may be the danger.

chapters.title: The Crevasse Field
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A hidden crevasse nearly takes Tomas; Hazel's rope work saves him, and the near-death cracks the team open — stories shared over the stove, including fragments of Hazel's disgrace. Beat: fragile trust forged in shared mortality.

chapters.title: The Cave Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Dorje's POV. Following a meltwater echo, Dorje finds a cave mouth behind the seracs. Inside: the survey team's instruments arranged deliberately around a wall of ancient ice holding something dark and human-shaped. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Frozen Testimony
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The ice holds bodies — decades old, in colonial-era uniforms, bound and shot. The Meridian Survey didn't vanish; it found a massacre preserved in the glacier, evidence of a purge the state never acknowledged. Beat: the mystery resolves into a moral bomb.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Kwan's POV. A gaunt man emerges from a higher ice shelf: Dr. Elias Vann, Meridian's geologist, half-frozen and paranoid, clutching film canisters and a journal. He trusts no one — least of all anyone sent by Rathore. Beat: the mission gains its living heart and its heaviest burden.

chapters.title: Two Sets of Orders
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Confronted by Hazel, Priya admits her contingency orders and reveals the radio was sabotaged before departure — Rathore never intended a rescue. Torn between career and conscience, she burns her orders. Beat: betrayal confessed; allegiance shifts.

chapters.title: Vann's Journal
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Reading Vann's account by headlamp: the survey documented the massacre site, radioed the ministry, and were told to wait. Then armed men came at night; Vann alone crawled into the ice caves. Beat: grief and fury; Hazel sees her own scapegoating mirrored in his.

chapters.title: The Cleanup Crew Arrives
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Helicopters. Six armed men in unmarked gear descend toward the cave, led by a man carrying Rathore's authority. The team scatters into whiteout with Vann and the evidence. Beat: the chase begins; the mountain turns hostile on schedule.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Storm-bound in a snow cave, the group debates: split up so someone escapes with the film, or stay together and risk all. Hazel argues for the rope-team rule — no one left behind — the rule she broke seven years ago. Beat: redemption theme made explicit under mortal stakes.

chapters.title: The Amulet's Debt
chapters.summary: Dorje's POV. Guiding them through the storm by memory and the old woman's amulet, Dorje reveals his grandfather was among the massacred porters whose deaths the ice preserves. This mountain is family ground. Beat: personal history fuses with the plot; the debt comes due.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Icefall
chapters.summary: Kwan's POV. The cleanup crew corners them at the icefall. Kwan holds the route with flares and nerve while the others cross a collapsing serac bridge; Priya is shot shielding Vann. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of truth paid in blood.

chapters.title: Rathore's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Rathore, arrived by helicopter below the icefall, offers Hazel everything she lost — licenses restored, record cleared — for Vann and the film. For one long moment she wants it more than air. Beat: the darkest hour is temptation, not violence.

chapters.title: No One Left Behind
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel refuses, and instead of fleeing, leads the crew onto the rotten glacier where their weight does what bullets couldn't — the ice gives way beneath the armed men. She carries the wounded Priya down through the breaking monsoon. Beat: climax; skill, guilt, and principle converge.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The battered party reaches the last village as the monsoon breaks fully. The old woman receives Dorje like returning blood; villagers bar the road against any pursuit. Vann, feverish but alive, entrusts the film to Hazel. Beat: sanctuary, exhaustion, and the weight of choice ahead.

chapters.title: The Story Gets Out
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In Rungli, Hazel hands the film and journal to a journalist waiting on Rathore's own paper trail, then surrenders to the police rather than run. Interrogation scenes intercut with headlines breaking: the massacre confirmed, Rathore implicated. Beat: justice outside the law achieved at the price of freedom.

chapters.title: When the Monsoon Wakes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Months later, awaiting trial, Hazel is visited by Vann, recovered, testifying on her behalf; charges unravel as the scandal widens. She doesn't know yet whether she'll guide again — only that she stopped counting miles. Final image: rain on the prison window, the mountain washed clean. Beat: identity reclaimed; quiet, earned hope.
